description:
Hi! We are Galaxy Rangers, a passionate high school team tackling the "Earth Analogs for Moon & Mars Bases" challenge. We bring strong skills in Coding, Web Development, Games, and Graphic Design to build an interactive 3D web/game platform comparing Earth and planetary data.

We're looking for teammates with Earth/Planetary Science, Data Analysis, or Storytelling skills to help analyze NASA datasets and craft our pitch. Let's innovate and explore space together!
summary:
AstroAnalog 3D is an interactive web and simulation platform created by Team Galaxy Rangers to identify and visualize Earth locations that serve as high-fidelity analogs for permanent Moon bases and Mars habitats.

To solve this challenge, we integrated open NASA planetary telemetry and Earth observation datasets—comparing key environmental parameters such as elevation, extreme temperature ranges, solar illumination, and mineral composition. Users can select target extraterrestrial zones like the Lunar South Pole or Martian craters to dynamically discover matching Earth training sites (such as the Antarctic Dry Valleys, Hawaiian lava tubes, and the Atacama Desert) through interactive 3D terrain visualizations and mission-readiness simulations.

This tool is vital because testing rovers, habitats, and astronaut workflows in accurate terrestrial analogs drastically reduces mission costs and risks before humanity returns to the Moon and ventures to Mars, while making space exploration engaging for students and researchers worldwide.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

AstroAnalog 3D is an interactive web and simulation platform built to identify Earth locations that best replicate the environmental and geological conditions of permanent Moon base candidates and Mars exploration zones. Users select an extraterrestrial target—such as the Lunar South Pole or Martian craters—and our Similarity Scoring Engine evaluates four core parameters: topography/elevation, extreme temperature ranges, solar illumination angles, and surface mineral composition. The platform then displays top-matching terrestrial analogs (such as the Antarctic Dry Valleys, Hawaiian lava tubes, and the Atacama Desert) through a split-screen 3D terrain explorer and a gamified mission-readiness simulation.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Launching hardware and astronauts to the Moon and Mars carries immense cost and risk. By pinpointing high-fidelity Earth training grounds, space agencies and researchers can test rovers, radiation-shielded habitats, and life-support systems safely before launch. Furthermore, our gamified interface makes complex planetary telemetry intuitive and engaging for students and the global public.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Web & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js / WebGL for interactive 3D terrain rendering.

- Data Processing: Python (Pandas, NumPy) for normalizing NASA elevation, temperature, and spectral datasets.

- Design & Prototyping: Canva, Figma, and standard graphic design tools for UI/UX and pitch presentation.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Unlike static spreadsheets or dense scientific papers, our project bridges planetary science with game-style interactivity—allowing users to test rover battery drain and thermal survival under real analog weather constraints. Key factors considered by Team Galaxy Rangers included multi-parameter weighting (e.g., prioritizing solar access for permanent Moon bases vs. regolith chemistry for Mars), accessibility for non-specialists, and strict adherence to open NASA datasets.
